### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e1dde1a5c15566bcc24d6c641b53d8282fcf655b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d5e5e482cf5335a1be4044826217b56e3551f792` — the merge of head `824e0f5d9021a0ee063dd1b133235c433fd089e9` into base `e1dde1a5c15566bcc24d6c641b53d8282fcf655b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d5e5e482cf5335a1be4044826217b56e3551f792 && git checkout d5e5e482cf5335a1be4044826217b56e3551f792
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e1dde1a5c15566bcc24d6c641b53d8282fcf655b 824e0f5d9021a0ee063dd1b133235c433fd089e9 && git checkout -B drift-repro e1dde1a5c15566bcc24d6c641b53d8282fcf655b && git merge --no-ff 824e0f5d9021a0ee063dd1b133235c433fd089e9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e1dde1a5c15566bcc24d6c641b53d8282fcf655b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e1dde1a5c15566bcc24d6c641b53d8282fcf655b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Seat ACCEPT · PR #28037 · head `824e0f5d9021a0ee063dd1b133235c433fd089e9` · 2026-10-30T10:18Z

## 维护者速读

A `connector_action` dispatch to a degraded connector used to end with "the platform retries automatically", even for an instance the platform does not retry. Now a **held** instance names its fix. A configuration fault met on a retry (#27992), or a credential written into the declaration that the upstream refused, gets "until its declaration is edited". A stored credential the upstream refused (#27237) gets "until credential '<ref>' is set again". Only an instance on the backoff keeps "retries automatically". The connectors page gains the failure-modes row for a configuration fault met on a retry.

## 席位核对

- **Shape:** draft → main, `Fixes #28016`, 8 files: `plugin-extension-api.ts`, `engine.ts`, `plugin.ts`, `builtin/connector-nodes.ts`, `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` (one row), two test files, and a changeset (`@objectstack/service-automation` patch). All are inside the claimed surface.
  - `check-governed-merges --pr 28037`: NOT governed, +334 / −14.
- **Read of the diff:** the engine's degraded record carries an optional `degradedHold` (`declaration` | `credential` + `ref`), through an optional 5th argument to `registerDegradedConnector` and a new reader, `getConnectorDegradedHold`. The two held paths in `plugin.ts` pass it: the #27992 configuration hold, and the #27237 credential hold, as `credential` when the value was stored through the door and `declaration` otherwise. The refusal and the engine's DEGRADED warning share one clause builder (`describeHold`). The credential `ref` is the declared reference name, never a value. A trailing full stop on the reason is no longer doubled.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch. The new engine surface is optional and additive only, with nothing narrowed, so no contract review is owed.
- **Serial:** open PR #27951 also edits `service-automation/src/engine.ts`. The hunks here (≈667, ≈4001, ≈4018, ≈4165) do not overlap its resume-path hunks (≈6373–6594), as shown in the PR body.
- **Tests:** a refusal pin for each hold kind, and the backoff control keeps "retries automatically". The card thread reports 4 of 29 red on `main`, three ablations each red, and a clean restore.
- **Out of surface:** `docs/adr/0097-declarative-connector-instances.md:186-190` still quotes "the platform retries automatically" for every husk. It is governed and is carried by #28038 for a governed approver.
- **Local (card thread):** package suite 224 files green, 92 of 92 derived gate families run with 0 NOT MEASURED, and `pnpm lint` and typecheck exit 0.
- **Gate check-runs on this head:** 50 total, 38 success, 12 skipped by the path filter, 0 failed. `mergeable_state: clean`.
- **Landing:** Tier S, under the maintainer's landing grant for this term (2026-10-29 22:05Z, seat thread). Ready + auto-merge through the relay.
